# Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP)

> The senior cloud security certification — architecture, data protection, infrastructure, application security, operations, and the legal and risk side that most technical certifications leave out entirely.

**ISC2** · code `CCSP` · **$599 USD** · 3 hours · pass 700 out of 1000 points · valid 3 years (three-year certification cycle, 90 CPE credits) · updated 2026-08-17

The CCSP is the cloud security certification that hiring managers recognise without explanation, and the one technical candidates most often underestimate — because a third of it is not technical at all.

## What the weights tell you to study

Cloud Data Security is the largest domain at 20%, and it is the most misread. Engineers arrive fluent in one provider's encryption options and find questions about the data lifecycle, tokenisation, information rights management and retention policy — vendor-neutral vocabulary that has to be learned deliberately.

The rest sits close together: Architecture, Platform and Infrastructure and Operations at 17% each, Application Security at 16%. There is no domain you can afford to skip, and no domain that dominates. Even coverage is the correct strategy.

Legal, Risk and Compliance is the smallest at 13% and the one that decides passes. Jurisdiction, e-discovery, contract design and privacy regimes cannot be reasoned out from engineering knowledge. They have to be memorised, and technical candidates reliably run out of patience before they are.

**Note the outline date.** These weights come from the exam outline that took effect on **1 August 2026**. Study material written against the previous outline is now describing a slightly different exam, and the AI/ML sub-domains in Domains 1 and 2 are new — check the publication date of anything you buy.

## What the exam is actually like

**Three hours, 100 to 150 items, scored 700 out of 1000.** The scoring is scaled and compensatory, so a strong domain can offset a weak one — but only if you answered. There is no penalty for guessing and no way to recover an unanswered item.

**The questions want the best answer, not the correct one.** Two options will usually both work. The one that scores is the one a risk manager would sign off: policy before tooling, contract before configuration, the control that is auditable over the control that is clever. Candidates who argue with this pattern rather than learning it are the ones who resit.

## Where the marks are lost

Answering as an engineer. The exam consistently rewards governance thinking, and the most common failure is a strong practitioner picking the technically superior answer over the one the framework prescribes.

## Before you book

The exam costs $599 in the Americas, and the certification runs on a three-year cycle with 90 CPE credits and an annual maintenance fee — a recurring commitment, not a one-off purchase. Confirm the experience requirement before you pay: without it you can still pass and hold Associate of ISC2 status while you accrue it, but that is a decision worth making on purpose.

## What the exam weights

The blueprint decides where study time goes. These are the published weights.

| Domain | Weight | |
|---|---:|---|
| Cloud Data Security | 20% | `████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░` |
| Cloud Concepts, Architecture and Design | 17% | `███░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░` |
| Cloud Platform and Infrastructure Security | 17% | `███░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░` |
| Cloud Security Operations | 17% | `███░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░` |
| Cloud Application Security | 16% | `███░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░` |
| Legal, Risk and Compliance | 13% | `███░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░` |

<details><summary><b>Cloud Concepts, Architecture and Design</b> — 17%</summary>

- Understand cloud computing concepts
- Describe cloud reference architecture
- Understand security concepts relevant to cloud computing
- Understand design principles of secure cloud computing
- Evaluate cloud service providers (CSP)
- Comprehend artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML)

</details>

<details><summary><b>Cloud Data Security</b> — 20%</summary>

- Describe cloud data concepts
- Design and implement cloud data storage architectures
- Design and apply data security technologies and strategies
- Implement data discovery
- Plan and implement data classification
- Design and implement information rights management (IRM)
- Plan and implement data retention, deletion and archiving policies
- Design and implement auditability, traceability and accountability of data events
- Comprehend data protection of AI and ML data

</details>

<details><summary><b>Cloud Platform and Infrastructure Security</b> — 17%</summary>

- Comprehend cloud infrastructure and platform components
- Design a secure data centre
- Analyze risks associated with cloud infrastructure and platforms
- Plan and implementation of security controls
- Plan business continuity (BC) and disaster recovery (DR)

</details>

<details><summary><b>Cloud Application Security</b> — 16%</summary>

- Advocate training and awareness for application security
- Describe the secure software development life cycle (SDLC) process
- Apply the secure software development life cycle (SDLC)
- Apply cloud software assurance and validation
- Use verified secure software
- Comprehend and apply the specifics of cloud application architecture
- Design appropriate identity and access management (IAM) solutions

</details>

<details><summary><b>Cloud Security Operations</b> — 17%</summary>

- Build and implement physical and logical infrastructure for cloud environment
- Operate and maintain physical and logical infrastructure for cloud environment
- Implement operational controls and standards
- Support digital forensics
- Manage communication with relevant parties
- Manage security operations

</details>

<details><summary><b>Legal, Risk and Compliance</b> — 13%</summary>

- Articulate legal requirements and unique risks within the cloud environment
- Understand privacy issues
- Understand audit process, methodologies and required adaptations for a cloud environment
- Understand implications of cloud to enterprise risk management
- Understand outsourcing and cloud contract design

</details>

## Before you book it

- Five years of paid IT experience, three in information security and one in a CCSP domain (or sit as an Associate of ISC2)
- Working knowledge of at least one major cloud provider

## How to prepare

6 steps, **about 126 hours** in total.

### 1. Check the experience requirement before you spend anything

<sub>**~2 hours**</sub>

CCSP needs five years of paid IT experience, three of them in information security and one in a CCSP domain. Without it you can still sit the exam and become an Associate of ISC2 while you accrue the rest — but decide that deliberately rather than discovering it at endorsement.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 2, of which 2 free</summary>

- [CCSP certification requirements](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/ccsp) <sub>ISC2 · certification · free</sub>
- [CCSP Exam Outline (effective 1 August 2026)](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/ccsp/ccsp-certification-exam-outline) <sub>ISC2 · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

### 2. Read the outline as a checklist, not as background

<sub>**~4 hours**</sub>

Every sub-domain begins with a verb — understand, design, evaluate, implement — and that verb is the depth you are expected to reach. 'Comprehend cloud infrastructure components' and 'design a secure data centre' are not the same amount of study, and the outline is telling you so.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 2, of which 2 free</summary>

- [CCSP Exam Outline (effective 1 August 2026)](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/ccsp/ccsp-certification-exam-outline) <sub>ISC2 · documentation · free</sub>
- [Cloud Security Alliance Security Guidance v5](https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/guidance) <sub>Cloud Security Alliance · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

### 3. Work Cloud Data Security first — it is the largest domain

<sub>**~35 hours**</sub>

At 20% it outweighs every other domain, and it is the one where vendor experience misleads: the exam asks about the data lifecycle, tokenisation, IRM and retention policy rather than about a particular provider's encryption menu. Learn the vocabulary the outline uses.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 3, of which 2 free</summary>

- [CSA Cloud Controls Matrix](https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/cloud-controls-matrix) <sub>Cloud Security Alliance · documentation · free</sub>
- [NIST SP 800-145 — The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/145/final) <sub>NIST · documentation · free</sub>
- **Practical Cloud Security** <sub>Chris Dotson · book · paid</sub> — free alternative: [AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/welcome.html)

</details>

### 4. Do not skip Legal, Risk and Compliance

<sub>**~20 hours**</sub>

It is the smallest domain at 13% and the one technical candidates fail on. Jurisdiction, e-discovery, cloud contract design and privacy regimes are unfamiliar and cannot be reasoned out from engineering knowledge — this is memorisation, and it is where an otherwise strong candidate loses a pass.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 3, of which 3 free</summary>

- [NIST SP 800-144 — Guidelines on Security and Privacy in Public Cloud Computing](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/144/final) <sub>NIST · documentation · free</sub>
- [EU GDPR full text](https://gdpr-info.eu/) <sub>gdpr-info.eu · documentation · free</sub>
- [NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — Security and Privacy Controls](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final) <sub>NIST · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

### 5. Cover the four remaining domains in weight order

<sub>**~45 hours**</sub>

Architecture, Platform and Infrastructure, Operations and Application Security together carry 67%. None is dominant, which makes even coverage the right strategy — the compensatory scoring means a strong domain can rescue a weak one, but only if nothing has been left blank.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 3, of which 3 free</summary>

- [NIST SP 800-210 — General Access Control Guidance for Cloud Systems](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/210/final) <sub>NIST · documentation · free</sub>
- [OWASP Top 10](https://owasp.org/www-project-top-ten/) <sub>OWASP · documentation · free</sub>
- [CSA Top Threats to Cloud Computing](https://cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/topics/top-threats) <sub>Cloud Security Alliance · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

### 6. Practise the question style, not just the material

<sub>**~20 hours**</sub>

ISC2 items are scenario-based and often have two defensible answers, one of which is better. Train the habit of asking what a risk manager would choose rather than what an engineer would build — that single reframing moves more marks than another pass through the material.

<details><summary><b>Resources</b> — 2, of which 2 free</summary>

- [CCSP exam registration and Pearson VUE scheduling](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/ccsp/ccsp-exam) <sub>ISC2 · certification · free</sub>
- [ISC2 Exam Pricing](https://www.isc2.org/register-for-exam/isc2-exam-pricing) <sub>ISC2 · documentation · free</sub>

</details>

## Questions

<details><summary><b>Is the CCSP exam hard?</b></summary><br>

It is hard in a way technical candidates do not expect: the material itself is not obscure, but a third of it is not technical at all. The exam rewards governance thinking over engineering thinking, and strong practitioners who pick the technically superior answer instead of the one a risk manager would sign off are the ones who resit.

</details>

<details><summary><b>What domains does the CCSP exam cover, and what should I study first?</b></summary><br>

Cloud Data Security is the largest domain at 20% and should come first — it covers vendor-neutral vocabulary like the data lifecycle, tokenisation, information rights management and retention policy, which trips up engineers fluent in only one provider's tooling. Architecture, Platform and Infrastructure and Operations follow at 17% each, Application Security at 16%, and Legal, Risk and Compliance at 13%.

</details>

<details><summary><b>Where do most candidates lose points on the CCSP exam?</b></summary><br>

The most common failure is answering as an engineer rather than a risk manager: the exam consistently rewards governance thinking, and picking the technically superior answer over the one the framework prescribes costs marks. Legal, Risk and Compliance compounds this — it is the smallest domain at 13%, but jurisdiction, e-discovery, contract design and privacy regimes cannot be reasoned out from engineering knowledge and have to be memorised.

</details>

<details><summary><b>How much does the CCSP exam cost, and how long is it valid?</b></summary><br>

The exam costs $599 USD in the Americas region, per ISC2's pricing page. The certification runs on a three-year cycle that requires 90 CPE credits plus an annual maintenance fee, so it is a recurring commitment rather than a one-off purchase.

</details>

<details><summary><b>Do I need five years of experience before I can get CCSP certified?</b></summary><br>

CCSP requires five years of paid IT experience, three of them in information security and one in a CCSP domain. If you don't have it yet, you can still sit the exam and hold Associate of ISC2 status while you accrue the rest — but the prep path recommends deciding that deliberately rather than discovering the gap at endorsement.

</details>

<details><summary><b>What format is the CCSP exam, and what score do I need to pass?</b></summary><br>

The CCSP is a three-hour exam with 100 to 150 multiple choice and advanced items, taken at a Pearson VUE test centre, and the pass mark is 700 out of 1000 points. Scoring is scaled and compensatory, meaning a strong domain can offset a weak one, but only for items you actually answered — there's no penalty for guessing and no way to recover a blank item.

</details>
